{"description":"COMPARE-AND-SWAP ON THE WRITE PATH. `create_node` accepts `expected_content_hash`; supply what you read and the write is REFUSED when the node has moved since, naming both hashes. Omit it and the old behaviour is unchanged. In the core: `upsert_node_if_unchanged`, with `node_content_hash` as the canonical hash.

THE FAILURE, measured from BOTH SIDES of one collision on a shared graph: a worker read a node, ninety seconds later another attached session wrote it, the write returned a normal success with the full node body, and THE WINNER WAS NEVER TOLD. The loser found out only because `record_change` happens to return the snapshot it took — a diagnostic side-effect of an unrelated tool, not a guard.

⭐ WHY A REFUSAL RATHER THAN A FIFTH REPORT, and this is `rule:fix-it-properly-while-it-is-still-cheap` deciding the shape. The `revision` block already REPORTED what a write replaced — that is detection, it tells the loser afterwards and tells the winner nothing. The requirement's own words were that the block's hash "is exactly the raw material a compare-and-swap needs; nothing consumes it yet". This consumes it. Another report would have been the workaround.

FOUR DESIGN CALLS, each with its reason:
(1) IT GUARDS THE UPSERT, NOT THE RAW CREATE. The upsert is the merge path every surface writes through; a guard on a path nobody calls reports success and defends nothing.
(2) ABSENT IS A MISMATCH, NOT A CREATE. If the node is gone, somebody DELETED it while the caller was deciding, and silently recreating it would undo their removal — the same silent loss pointed the other way. Refused with its own message.
(3) THE HASH MOVED INTO THE CORE. The MCP surface computed it for the `revision` block; the moment it became a PRECONDITION, two implementations of one number became a way for a caller's correct expectation to be refused by an engine that agreed with them — and the divergence would appear only under contention, the one condition nobody tests by hand.
(4) OPT-IN. A caller who never read the node has no honest expectation to state, and making it mandatory would break every existing writer — a worse defect than the one being fixed.

⚠️⚠️ AND IT SHIPPED BROKEN FOR ONE COMMIT, CAUGHT ONLY BY DRIVING THE REAL SURFACE. Generic `create_node` carried NO `revision` block at all — the block was attached by the TYPED constructors and never by it. So the compare-and-swap existed with its precondition value UNOBTAINABLE FROM THE VERY TOOL THAT DEMANDED IT. Every core test passed. The MCP probe failed on its first run, at the line that reads `revision.prior_content_hash`. `create_node` now returns the block. This is AGENTS.md's "compiling is not the finish line, and neither is a green unit test" earning its place for the second time in two days.

MUTATION-CHECKED RATHER THAN TRUSTED: discarding the guard's refusal makes exactly the two probes that should fail, fail (stale read, deleted node), while the counterweight and the hash-stability probe correctly survive — so the suite is not vacuous in the way `dec:non-goal-reflow2-does-not-judge-whether-a-check-is-meaningful` says reflow2 cannot detect for you.

⚠️ HONEST BOUND, and it is the next question rather than a defect: the TYPED constructors (`add_decision`, `add_requirement`, `add_capability`, …) still merge with no expectation available. They are the commonest write path in practice, so the hole this closes is real but partial. Whether they should carry the parameter too is not settled — it is ~10 more surface changes, and the case for it is exactly the case made here.","name":"A write can be made conditional on what the caller read, so a lost update is refused rather than reported afterwards","provenance":"authored","status":"realized"}
